title: Conserve Mode Playbook — Experiment Grid & Rollout Plan
creator: Sofia Kim
description:
Objective: Create a repeatable playbook and prioritized experiment grid for 'Conserve Mode' — a set of runtime policies and model variants that reduce per-token unit cost while respecting latency SLOs and quality budgets. This ticket tracks cross-functional work to define hypotheses, instrumentation, rollout criteria, and automation steps for progressively enabling batching, prefix caching, and quantized model variants across hosted and dedicated surfaces.

Scope:
- Produce a hypothesis-driven experiment matrix covering request shaping, dynamic batching thresholds, KV cache TTL policies, and two levels of quantized model variants (Q4_0 and Q5_0).
- Define metric guardrails (latency P95, normalized quality delta on evals, token cost delta) and automated golden-check blocking rules.
- Build an initial field trial for 3 pilot customers + internal traffic lanes, including rollout plan and rollback criteria.
- Deliver a one-page playbook and console runbook snippets for SRE/solutions engineers to enable/disable Conserve Mode per-customer.

Why now: With rising inference spend in Q1 and multiple requests from enterprise pilots for cost controls, we need an operational, low-risk way to surface adaptive economies to customers without sacrificing reliability or product experience.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment matrix defined with clear hypotheses and success thresholds for each cell (batch size, batching timeout, KV TTL, quant variant)
Instrumentation dashboards created (token-cost, P95 latency, quality regression signal) with alert thresholds and runbook links
Field trial config and canary policy documented in the Console runbook; at least 3 pilot customers enrolled and consented
Automated gating implemented: experiments that exceed quality regression or latency guardrails are auto-disabled and create a ticket
Playbook doc published in Confluence and linked to the product status board
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff meeting with Eng (serving/runtime), SRE, and Solutions. Agreed to focus on two quant variants and conservative batching defaults for initial trials.

2025-02-21: Data snapshot: identified 12 workload archetypes by sequence-length and concurrency—prioritized three archetypes for pilots (chat medium-length, search short-length, summarization long-length).
2025-02-28: Instrumentation spike completed. Prototype dashboards in Grafana (token-cost vs latency) and a lightweight regression harness against canonical prompt set created.
2025-03-01: Drafted hypothesis matrix and initial canary policy. Waiting on legal for pilot customer consent template. Action: Solutions to identify pilot customers by 2025-03-07.
2025-03-03: Engineering proposed a fallback policy that automatically routes to unquantized model if P95 latency exceeds threshold for two consecutive windows. Added to acceptance criteria.
